ca_dino_s_egg.blurb: Dino's Egg is a single big, rounded boulder in the Outback, the open valley just north of the Hidden Valley campground in Joshua Tree National Park. Its mottled brown and tan surface gives it the look of a giant egg, and the face on the west side is speckled with dark patina. Twelve boulder problems circle it, and the spread leans easy: about a third are the gentlest grade, a quarter are V0, and the rest are V2 with a couple of V4 lines. That makes it a friendly stop for newer boulderers, and for anyone warming up before heading to harder blocks nearby. The usual way down is the west arete.

ca_hummingbird_boulders.blurb: Hummingbird Boulders is a small bouldering spot on Bishop Peak, the volcanic plug above San Luis Obispo on the Central Coast. Just two boulders hold the dozen problems here, each with a couple of standout lines. The grades start around V2 and V3, with a handful in the middle and a notable group at V6, plus two V8s, so it suits stronger boulderers more than beginners. Reach it by a faint trail that leaves the fire road a little above the Pete and Chlorissa boulders. Other Bishop Peak boulders sit along the same trail, so it combines easily into a longer session.

ca_fisherman_s_buttress_east_face.blurb: The east face of Fisherman's Buttress is a roadside wall on the south shore of Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, at nearly 7,000 feet. Twelve routes run from 5.9 into the low 5.12s: seven sport lines, four trad and one top-rope, with most of the grades clustered in the 5.10s and 5.11s. The climbing is short, thin and technical, and some lines still carry lichen. Because the wall faces east it catches the morning sun and drops into shade by afternoon, which helps on warm days. A few small pullouts serve the whole crag, so expect to share the space.
ca_fisherman_s_buttress_east_face.approach: A faint trail winds through boulders from the roadside pullouts, passes Three Fishes Rock and reaches the base of the face. It is a short walk.

ca_habanero_the.blurb: The Habanero is a large square block among the Separate Boulders, at the base of Queen Mountain in the Wastelands of Joshua Tree National Park. Its varnished rock offers wide views over Queen Valley, and problems are spread across the east, south, southwest and west faces. Twelve boulder problems are listed, and most are easy: nearly half are the lowest grade, a quarter are V0, and singles run from V1 up to V4 on the namesake line. It is a decent objective for a mixed group wanting short, simple problems after a longer walk in, rather than a destination for hard testpieces.

ca_patagonia_pile_east_face.blurb: The east face of Patagonia Pile is an overhanging wall in the Outback area of Joshua Tree National Park, easy to spot from Hidden Valley campground. It is steep, and mostly trad, with three top-rope lines, and it has very few easy routes to warm up on. Nearly all of the twelve routes are 5.11, with a single 5.10 and two 5.12s, so it suits climbers who already lead the grade. The face looks east, so it gets the morning sun and cools off in the afternoon. The base is mostly flat, which makes it comfortable for a day with a group.
ca_patagonia_pile_east_face.approach: From Hidden Valley campground walk north, past the Iron Door Cave area and the east end of The Blob, then aim for the overhanging face across easy boulders to a mostly flat base.

ca_higher_wall.blurb: Higher Wall is the upper tier of the 4:20 Wall at Rock Creek, in the Eastern Sierra near Mammoth Lakes, at roughly 9,350 feet. The wall stands above the Lower Wall and stretches out to its right, with single pitches of about 15 to 30 metres or more. Twelve routes mix trad and sport: mostly 5.10s and 5.11s, with one 5.9 and one third-class line. Moves tend to be balancy, technical and sometimes hard to read, rather than powerful. Loose rock is a real concern, so wear a helmet and avoid climbing when another party is directly below. The altitude and the quieter alpine feel set it apart from lower crags.
ca_higher_wall.approach: The wall is reached from the Lower Wall below: either top out one of its routes, or scramble a narrow third-class gully along the right side of the Lower Wall.

ca_el_cariso_misc_problems.blurb: This is a grab bag of twelve climbs at El Cariso, a secluded granite boulder field in the Santa Ana Mountains where Orange and Riverside Counties meet, at around 3,000 feet. Eight are boulder problems, spanning an easy warm-up through the V2 to V5 range with one very hard outlier, plus three sport lines, a short crack and some slab climbing at moderate grades. These are the lines not yet filed under a particular boulder, ordered roughly left to right from the closest to the car, with another cluster on a hill to the west. It is a quiet spot, and sound carries, so keep voices down.

ca_east_face_14.blurb: The East Face of Moro Rock is a big granite dome wall in Sequoia National Park, at about 5,750 feet, above the Giant Forest. Twelve routes are listed, and many are multi-pitch lines. The mix is trad, bolted sport lines and several aid climbs, with the free grades running from easy fifth class through the 5.10s and into one 5.12. Expect long days on a big face that gets far less traffic online than comparable Yosemite walls, and note that the walk starts on the summit staircase before a climbers' trail leads off to a ledge along the wall.
